correctness.rationale: The Petersen graph is connected and has no triangles or four-cycles. Two disjoint odd cycles must partition its ten vertices, so a joining edge exists and the edge semigroup is normal. Alternating sums along even walks give all vertex-coordinate differences (an odd closed detour adjusts parity), and adding an edge gives the full even-sum lattice. For the coordinate facets, deleting 45 leaves the five-cycle 12,34,15,24,35 and every remaining vertex attaches to this cycle; transitivity handles all deletions. Independent sets are intersecting families of two-subsets. A singleton leaves a bipartite six-vertex remainder, a pair a nonempty three-vertex remainder, and a three-element star a one-vertex remainder. The other triple type is the triangle on three labels, namely N(v) for the complementary pair; it and each four-element star have full coverage and connected cross-edge graph. Hence the facet criterion gives exactly the stated 25 inequalities. Normal canonical interior monomials are 1+b with b>=0 and even sum 2r, and their minimality is exactly nonremovability of any positive-support edge. The canonical module is Cohen–Macaulay; graded local duality gives top local cohomology dual to R, with end degree 0, so regularity is 10 and no minimal generator after degree 10 is possible. An independent exact stars-and-bars enumeration with tight-facet forbidden edges gave interior/minimal counts (1,1), (15,0), (130,10), (760,0), (3345,0), (11953,0) and verified the ten closed-neighborhood offsets. The rank-ten ring gives projective dimension nine; label permutations act on the displayed generators as claimed, with the characteristic-zero two-subset module decomposing by the Young rule.
residual_risks: The permutation action is the specified action on the ideal, not a claim about a canonical choice of geometric linearization.

evidence: The prior criterion gives type 11 and nonlevelness. The normalized canonical module has reversed numerator; subtracting the numerator of R (via the injection of R generated by the single bottom-degree element) yields 10t^2-10t^3. The quotient vanishes in normalized degrees 0 and 1 and has dimension ten in degree 2, so the type forces one degree-five and ten degree-seven generators, with no others.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The numerical degree distribution needs no new search and is not credited as new. To go from it to the ideal one must construct ten distinct new monomials with those exponents and check interior status and nondivisibility: e.g. for q_v each four-element star meets N[v] in at most two vertices, and removing an edge of N[v] leaves two intersecting labels-as-vertices that violate the degree-six star constraint. This additional exact identification fixes the natural action; graded Hilbert and type invariants do not give it.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is a standard, symmetric nonbipartite example whose ordinary normal edge ring is already studied as almost Gorenstein but not level. Giving the exact canonical ideal as monomials, rather than recalculating type or graded data, identifies the selected symmetric realization and permits subsequent explicit equivariant or algebraic computations. The relevant invariant and graph are natural independently of the finite census.
residual_risks: No value is credited for a known type, h-vector, dimension, or generator-degree multiset by itself; the useful increment is the actual ideal and consequent explicit action.
